SYS-001.title: Operating system no longer supported
SYS-001.description: The installed version of Windows no longer receives security fixes from Microsoft.
SYS-001.danger: Every new flaw discovered in Windows will stay open forever on this computer. Attackers specifically target systems that are no longer patched.
SYS-001.impact: Permanent exposure to new vulnerabilities (ransomware, remote takeover). Not acceptable for professional use.
SYS-001.description_linux: The installed system version no longer receives security fixes from its vendor.
SYS-001.description_macos: The installed system version no longer receives security fixes from its vendor.
SYS-001.danger_linux: Every new flaw discovered will stay open forever on this computer. Attackers specifically target systems that are no longer patched.
SYS-001.danger_macos: Every new flaw discovered will stay open forever on this computer. Attackers specifically target systems that are no longer patched.
steps: Check whether the computer can run Windows 11 with the “PC Health Check” app.
Back up important data to an external drive or the cloud.
If the computer is compatible: Settings > Windows Update > Upgrade to Windows 11.
Otherwise: subscribe to Microsoft Extended Security Updates (ESU), replace the computer, or install a supported system (e.g. Linux).
steps_linux: Back up your data.
Upgrade to a supported version of the distribution.
Ubuntu: do-release-upgrade; Debian: point the APT sources to the new release, then apt full-upgrade.
steps_macos: Check whether the Mac supports the latest macOS (Apple website).
Back up with Time Machine.
System Settings > General > Software Update > Upgrade.

winver.attendu: Windows 11; “Windows 10 version 22H2” means: no more security updates.

start ms-settings:windowsupdate.effet: Opens Windows Update: if the computer is compatible, the “Upgrade to Windows 11” offer appears there.

cat /etc/os-release.effet: Shows the name and version of the distribution.
cat /etc/os-release.attendu: a version that is still supported (see endoflife.date)

sudo do-release-upgrade.effet: Starts the upgrade to the next Ubuntu release.
sudo do-release-upgrade.attention: Back up your data first. Allow an hour or more, with the computer plugged in.

sw_vers.attendu: a version still supported by Apple

open \"x-apple.systempreferences:com.app.effet: Opens System Settings > Software Update, where the upgrade is offered.

SYS-002.title: System support ends soon (less than 6 months)
SYS-002.description: The installed version of Windows will soon stop receiving fixes.
SYS-002.danger: After the end-of-support date, the computer will no longer be protected against new flaws.
SYS-002.impact: A risk that will become critical in the short term if nothing is planned.
SYS-002.description_linux: The installed system version will soon stop receiving fixes.
SYS-002.description_macos: The installed system version will soon stop receiving fixes.
steps: Plan the upgrade to the next Windows version before the date shown.
Install the feature update offered in Windows Update.

start ms-settings:windowsupdate.effet: Opens Windows Update to install the next version of Windows.

SYS-003.title: Windows updates waiting to be installed
SYS-003.description: Windows Update reports available updates that are not installed yet.
SYS-003.danger: Published fixes publicly reveal the flaws they correct: an unpatched computer becomes an easy target within days.
SYS-003.impact: Known, exploitable vulnerabilities on the computer.
SYS-003.description_linux: Updates are available but not installed yet.
SYS-003.description_macos: Updates are available but not installed yet.
steps: Open Settings > Windows Update.
Click “Check for updates”, then “Install”.
Restart the computer when Windows asks.
steps_linux: Refresh the package list, then install the updates.
Restart if the kernel was updated.
steps_macos: Open System Settings > General > Software Update.
Install the updates offered and restart.

start ms-settings:windowsupdate.effet: Opens Windows Update: then click “Check for updates” and “Install”.

UsoClient StartInteractiveScan.effet: Starts searching for and downloading updates, like the “Check for updates” button.
UsoClient StartInteractiveScan.attention: Restart the computer when Windows asks.

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade.effet: Downloads and installs all updates (answer “Y” to confirm).
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade.attention: Ubuntu / Debian. Fedora: sudo dnf upgrade --refresh

sudo softwareupdate -ia --restart.attention: Save your work: the computer restarts immediately.

SYS-004.title: No update installed recently
SYS-004.description: The last Windows update was installed more than 45 days ago.
SYS-004.danger: Microsoft publishes security fixes every month (“Patch Tuesday”). A gap of more than a month means updates are no longer being installed.
SYS-004.description_linux: No package update has been installed for more than 45 days.
SYS-004.description_macos: No update has been installed for more than 45 days.
SYS-004.danger_linux: Vendors publish security fixes continuously: a long period without installing any means updates are no longer applied.
SYS-004.danger_macos: Vendors publish security fixes continuously: a long period without installing any means updates are no longer applied.
steps: Open the Windows Update history and look for failed installs.
Check for updates and install them.
If installs keep failing, run the Windows Update troubleshooter.
steps_linux: Run a full package update.
Turn on automatic security updates (unattended-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu, dnf-automatic on Fedora/RHEL).

Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn -De.effet: Lists the 5 most recent updates with their install date.
Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn -De.attendu: a date less than 45 days old

start ms-settings:windowsupdate-history.effet: Opens the Windows Update history to spot failed installs.

UsoClient StartInteractiveScan.effet: Restarts the search for and installation of updates.

grep \" upgrade \" /var/log/dpkg.log | t.effet: Shows the latest package updates installed.

sudo apt install unattended-upgrades &&.effet: Turns on automatic installation of security updates (answer “Yes”).

SYS-005.title: User Account Control (UAC) disabled
SYS-005.description: UAC asks for confirmation before a program gets administrator rights. It is disabled on this computer.
SYS-005.danger: Any program you run, including malware, silently gets full control of the machine.
SYS-005.impact: Malware installed invisibly, system changes without any warning.
steps: Open Control Panel > User Accounts > Change User Account Control settings.
Set the slider to “Notify me only when apps try to make changes to my computer” (default level).
Confirm, then restart.

reg query \"HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\W.effet: Shows the state of User Account Control (UAC).

UserAccountControlSettings.effet: Opens the UAC settings: set the slider to the default level (2nd notch from the top).

Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\\SOFTWARE\.attention: Then restart the computer for the change to apply.

SYS-006.title: UAC set to never ask for confirmation
SYS-006.description: UAC is on but automatically elevates programs without asking administrators for confirmation.
SYS-006.danger: Malware can get administrator rights without any visible warning.
steps: Open the UAC settings (search “UAC” in the Start menu).
Move the slider back to the default or highest level.
Confirm.

reg query \"HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\W.effet: Shows the confirmation level asked of administrators.

UserAccountControlSettings.effet: Opens the UAC settings to move the slider back to the default level.

SYS-007.title: Secure Boot disabled
SYS-007.description: Secure Boot checks that only signed boot loaders run when the PC starts. It is disabled or unavailable.
SYS-007.danger: A “bootkit” can load before Windows and hide from the antivirus.
SYS-007.impact: A persistent compromise that is very hard to detect.
SYS-007.location: The computer's UEFI firmware (BIOS); can be checked in msinfo32 > “Secure Boot State”
SYS-007.danger_linux: A “bootkit” can load before the operating system and hide from security tools.
SYS-007.danger_macos: A “bootkit” can load before the operating system and hide from security tools.
steps: Check the state: run msinfo32 and read “Secure Boot State”.
Restart and enter the UEFI setup (often F10, F2 or Del at startup; F10 on HP).
In the Security or Boot tab, enable “Secure Boot” (the mode must be UEFI, not “Legacy/CSM”).
Save and restart. If the disk uses MBR, convert it to GPT first with mbr2gpt.
steps_linux: Enter the UEFI setup at startup and enable Secure Boot.
The signed kernels of Ubuntu, Fedora and Debian boot with Secure Boot; third-party drivers (NVIDIA, VirtualBox) must be signed via MOK.

msinfo32.effet: Opens “System Information”: read the “Secure Boot State” line.
msinfo32.attendu: On; “BIOS Mode: Legacy” = Secure Boot impossible without conversion

shutdown /r /fw /t 0.effet: Restarts straight into the UEFI (BIOS) settings to turn on “Secure Boot”.
shutdown /r /fw /t 0.attention: Save your work: the computer restarts immediately. Only works on PCs in UEFI mode.

ACC-001.title: Too many active administrator accounts
ACC-001.description: More than two active accounts are members of the Administrators group.
ACC-001.danger: Each administrator account is a door to full control of the computer. The more there are, the higher the risk of a stolen password.
ACC-001.location: Computer Management > Local Users and Groups > Groups > Administrators
steps: List the members: lusrmgr.msc > Groups > Administrators.
Remove the accounts that don't need administrator rights from the group.
Keep a single administrator account for maintenance.
steps_linux: List the members of the administration groups.
Remove the accounts that don't need sudo.
steps_macos: Open System Settings > Users & Groups.
For each account that doesn't need it, turn off “Allow this user to administer this computer”.

Get-LocalGroupMember -SID S-1-5-32-544.effet: Lists the accounts in the Administrators group.

lusrmgr.msc.effet: Opens “Local Users and Groups” (Windows Pro): Groups > Administrators.

Remove-LocalGroupMember -SID S-1-5-32-54.effet: Removes this account from the Administrators group.
Remove-LocalGroupMember -SID S-1-5-32-54.attention: Never remove the last administrator account, nor your own before another administrator account works.

remplacer.NOM_DU_COMPTE: the exact name of the account to remove, as shown by the check command (without the PC name in front)

getent group sudo wheel.effet: Lists the accounts allowed to use sudo.

sudo gpasswd -d NOM sudo.effet: Removes this account from the sudo group.
sudo gpasswd -d NOM sudo.attention: Keep at least one account that can use sudo.

remplacer.NOM: the name of the account to remove

sudo dseditgroup -o edit -d NOM -t user.effet: Removes administrator rights from this account.
sudo dseditgroup -o edit -d NOM -t user.attention: Keep at least one administrator account.

ACC-002.title: Guest account enabled
ACC-002.description: The built-in Windows Guest account is enabled.
ACC-002.danger: The Guest account lets anyone sign in without a personal password.
ACC-002.impact: Uncontrolled access to the computer and to network shares.
ACC-002.description_macos: The macOS “Guest User” account is enabled.
ACC-002.location_macos: System Settings > Users & Groups > Guest User
steps: Open lusrmgr.msc > Users.
Right-click “Guest” > Properties > check “Account is disabled”.
steps_macos: Open System Settings > Users & Groups.
Click “Guest User” and turn off “Allow guests to log in to this computer”.

Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID -l.effet: Shows the state of the Guest account.

defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.a.effet: Shows the state of the guest account.

ACC-003.title: Built-in Administrator account enabled
ACC-003.description: The built-in Administrator account (RID 500) is enabled. Every attacker knows it, and it is not subject to lockout.
ACC-003.danger: A favourite target of password brute-force attacks.
ACC-003.impact: Full takeover if the password is guessed.
steps: Make sure another administrator account works.
Disable the built-in Administrator account.

Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID -l.effet: Shows the state of the built-in Administrator account.

Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID -l.attention: First check that another administrator account works.

ACC-004.title: Active account without a required password
ACC-004.description: An active local account is not required to have a password.
ACC-004.danger: Anyone can sign in to this account without a password, locally or sometimes remotely.
ACC-004.impact: Direct access to the user's data.
steps: Set a strong password for the account (12 characters or more).
Make the password mandatory.
steps_linux: Set a password for the account, or lock it if it is not used.

Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name,Enabl.effet: Lists the accounts and whether they require a password.
Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name,Enabl.attendu: PasswordRequired : True for every enabled account

net user NOM_DU_COMPTE *.effet: Asks you to type a new password for this account (nothing appears while you type: that's normal).

remplacer.NOM_DU_COMPTE: the account name shown in the finding

net user NOM_DU_COMPTE /passwordreq:yes.effet: Makes a password mandatory for this account.

remplacer.NOM_DU_COMPTE: the account name shown in the finding

sudo awk -F: '($2 == \"\") {print $1}' /.effet: Lists the accounts without a password.

sudo passwd NOM.effet: Sets a password for this account.

remplacer.NOM: the account name shown in the finding

sudo passwd -l NOM.effet: Locks this account if it is not used.

remplacer.NOM: the account name shown in the finding

ACC-005.title: Administrator account used every day
ACC-005.description: The account used every day is a member of the Administrators group.
ACC-005.danger: Malware opened by mistake is only one UAC dialog away from full control.
ACC-005.impact: One wrong click can compromise the whole system.
steps: Create a separate administrator account reserved for maintenance.
Change the everyday account type to “Standard user”.
Enter the administrator credentials only when Windows asks.
steps_macos: Create an administrator account dedicated to maintenance.
Remove administrator rights from the account used every day.

Get-LocalGroupMember -SID S-1-5-32-544.effet: Checks whether your account is an administrator.
Get-LocalGroupMember -SID S-1-5-32-544.attendu: your account is not in the list

start ms-settings:otherusers.effet: Opens the accounts page to create a maintenance administrator account, then change the type of yours.

net user admin-maintenance * /add.effet: Creates the “admin-maintenance” account and asks for its password.

Add-LocalGroupMember -SID S-1-5-32-544 -.effet: Gives administrator rights to the maintenance account.
Add-LocalGroupMember -SID S-1-5-32-544 -.attention: Test the maintenance account BEFORE removing the rights of your everyday account.

open \"x-apple.systempreferences:com.app.effet: Opens Users & Groups to create a maintenance administrator account.

sudo dseditgroup -o edit -d NOM -t user.effet: Removes administrator rights from your everyday account.
sudo dseditgroup -o edit -d NOM -t user.attention: First create and test another administrator account.

NET-001.title: SMBv1 protocol enabled
NET-001.description: SMBv1 is the first version (1983) of the Windows file-sharing protocol. It is obsolete and disabled by default since Windows 10 1709.
NET-001.danger: SMBv1 was exploited by the WannaCry and NotPetya ransomware (EternalBlue flaw) to spread automatically from computer to computer.
NET-001.impact: Remote code execution without authentication, ransomware spreading across the network.
NET-001.location: Control Panel > Programs > Turn Windows features on or off > SMB 1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support
steps: Open “Turn Windows features on or off”.
Uncheck “SMB 1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support”.
Confirm and restart.

Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select-Obje.effet: Shows whether the SMBv1 protocol is enabled.

optionalfeatures.effet: Opens “Windows Features”: uncheck “SMB 1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support”.

Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -.attention: Windows then asks you to restart.

NET-002.title: Remote Desktop (RDP) enabled
NET-002.description: The computer accepts Remote Desktop connections.
NET-002.danger: RDP is one of the most attacked entry points (password brute force, flaws such as BlueKeep).
NET-002.impact: Remote takeover if a password is weak or a flaw exists.
steps: If Remote Desktop is not used: Settings > System > Remote Desktop > Off.
If it is needed: expose it only through a VPN, turn on NLA authentication and use strong passwords.

reg query \"HKLM\\System\\CurrentControl.effet: Shows whether Remote Desktop is enabled.

start ms-settings:remotedesktop.effet: Opens the “Remote Desktop” setting to turn it off.

Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\\System\\C.attention: If you are connected to this PC remotely, the connection will drop.

NET-003.title: Remote Desktop without Network Level Authentication (NLA)
NET-003.description: RDP is enabled without Network Level Authentication (NLA), which checks identity before opening a session.
NET-003.danger: An attacker reaches the sign-in screen and the RDP code without authenticating, which makes flaws easier to exploit.
NET-003.impact: Greater exposure to RDP flaws and denial-of-service attacks.
NET-003.location: Settings > System > Remote Desktop > Advanced settings
steps: Open the advanced Remote Desktop settings.
Check “Require computers to use Network Level Authentication to connect”.

reg query \"HKLM\\System\\CurrentControl.effet: Shows whether Network Level Authentication (NLA) is required.

SystemPropertiesRemote.effet: Opens the “Remote” system properties: check “…Network Level Authentication”.

Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\\System\\C.effet: Requires Network Level Authentication (NLA) for Remote Desktop.

NET-004.title: Sensitive service listening on all network interfaces
NET-004.description: A sensitive service (database, remote access, file transfer) accepts connections from any network address.
NET-004.danger: On a public network (café, school), other devices can try to connect to the service and exploit a flaw or a weak password.
NET-004.impact: Data leak or takeover of the service.
NET-004.location: The service's configuration (see the process shown)
steps: Identify the program shown (process column).
If it is not used, stop the service and disable its automatic start.
If it is only used locally, set its listening address to 127.0.0.1 (e.g. PostgreSQL: listen_addresses = 'localhost' in postgresql.conf).
Check that a firewall rule blocks this port on the Public profile.
steps_linux: Identify the service (process column).
If it is not used: stop and disable it.
If it is used locally: configure it to listen on 127.0.0.1.
Block the port in the firewall.
steps_macos: Identify the application (process column).
Quit it or turn off its network sharing in its preferences.
Turn on the macOS firewall.

netstat -ano | findstr :PORT.effet: Shows whether the port is open and the program's number (PID, last column).

remplacer.PORT: the port number shown in the finding (e.g. 5432)

tasklist /FI \"PID eq PID\".effet: Shows the name of the program using this port.

remplacer.PID: the program number (PID) shown in the finding

services.msc.effet: Opens the list of services: stop the service if it isn't used and set its startup to “Manual”.

New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'KMB -.effet: Blocks this port on public networks (café or school Wi-Fi…).

remplacer.PORT: the port number shown in the finding (e.g. 5432), in both places

sudo ss -tlnp | grep :PORT.effet: Shows whether the port is open and which program uses it.

remplacer.PORT: the port number shown in the finding

sudo systemctl disable --now SERVICE.effet: Stops the service and prevents it from starting again.

sudo ufw deny PORT/tcp.effet: Blocks this port in the firewall.

remplacer.PORT: the port number shown in the finding

sudo lsof -nP -iTCP:PORT -sTCP:LISTEN.effet: Shows which program listens on this port.

remplacer.PORT: the port number shown in the finding

NET-005.title: Folder shared on the network
NET-005.description: A non-administrative folder is shared on the network.
NET-005.danger: Depending on permissions, other network users can read, change or encrypt (ransomware) its contents.
steps: Open fsmgmt.msc > Shares.
Delete the share if it is no longer needed.
Otherwise, limit permissions to the users who need it (remove “Everyone”).
steps_linux: Remove unneeded shares from the configuration file.
Restrict allowed clients (NFS) or turn off guest access (Samba: guest ok = no).
Reload the service.

Get-SmbShare.attendu: only ADMIN$, C$ and IPC$ (default shares)

Get-SmbShareAccess -Name NOM_DU_PARTAGE.effet: Shows who can access the share.

remplacer.NOM_DU_PARTAGE: the share name shown in the finding

fsmgmt.msc.effet: Opens “Shared Folders” to stop the share or reduce access.

Remove-SmbShare -Name NOM_DU_PARTAGE -Fo.effet: Stops the share (the folder and its files are not deleted).

remplacer.NOM_DU_PARTAGE: the share name shown in the finding

sudo exportfs -v.effet: Lists the folders shared over NFS.

sudo nano /etc/exports.effet: Opens the NFS shares file: delete or restrict the line, then Ctrl+O, Enter, Ctrl+X.

sudo exportfs -ra.effet: Applies the changes to NFS shares.

sudo systemctl reload smbd.effet: Applies the changes to Samba shares (after editing /etc/samba/smb.conf).

FW-001.title: Windows firewall profile disabled
FW-001.description: Windows Firewall filters incoming connections. One of its profiles (Domain, Private or Public) is disabled.
FW-001.danger: On this type of network, every service on the computer can be reached directly by other devices.
FW-001.impact: Unauthorized connections reach the machine directly.
FW-001.description_linux: No firewall (ufw, firewalld, nftables) is active: every incoming connection reaches the services.
FW-001.description_macos: The macOS application firewall is off: applications can receive incoming connections without any check.
steps: Open Windows Settings.
Go to Windows Security.
Open “Firewall & network protection”.
Turn on the firewall for all three network profiles (Domain, Private, Public).
steps_linux: Ubuntu/Debian: enable ufw, allowing SSH first if you use it.
Fedora/RHEL: enable firewalld.
steps_macos: Open System Settings > Network > Firewall.
Turn on the firewall.

netsh advfirewall show allprofiles state.effet: Shows the firewall state for each network profile.

netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state.effet: Turns on the firewall for all 3 profiles (domain, private, public).

sudo ufw allow OpenSSH.attention: Only if you connect to this PC remotely over SSH.

sudo ufw enable.effet: Turns on the firewall (answer “y”). Fedora: sudo systemctl enable --now firewalld

FW-002.title: Incoming connections allowed by default
FW-002.description: The firewall lets through, by default, incoming connections that match no rule.
FW-002.danger: The firewall only blocks what is explicitly forbidden: every new service is exposed.
FW-002.location_macos: System Settings > Network > Firewall > Options (Block all incoming connections)
steps: Open wf.msc.
Click “Windows Defender Firewall Properties”.
For each profile, set “Inbound connections” to “Block (default)”.
steps_linux: Set the default incoming policy to “deny”.

Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object N.effet: Shows the default action for incoming connections.
Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object N.attendu: Block or NotConfigured for each profile

wf.msc.effet: Opens the advanced firewall: Properties > “Inbound connections: Block”.

FW-003.title: Inbound rule allows a sensitive port on the Public profile
FW-003.description: A firewall rule allows incoming connections to a sensitive port (file sharing, remote desktop, database) on public networks.
FW-003.danger: On public Wi-Fi, any device can reach this service.
steps: Open wf.msc > Inbound Rules.
Find the rule shown.
Disable it, or limit its profile to “Private” and its scope to the local subnet.

Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'NOM_DE.attendu: Enabled : False, or a profile other than Public

remplacer.NOM_DE_LA_REGLE: the rule name shown in the finding

wf.msc.effet: Opens the advanced firewall: Inbound Rules.

remplacer.NOM_DE_LA_REGLE: the rule name shown in the finding

AV-001.title: No active antivirus
AV-001.description: No active antivirus was detected on the computer.
AV-001.danger: Malware (viruses, ransomware, password stealers) can run without any detection.
AV-001.impact: Undetected infection, data loss or theft.
AV-001.description_linux: No antivirus was detected. On a Linux computer the risk is lower than on Windows, but still real (files shared with Windows computers, downloaded scripts).
steps: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection.
Turn on Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or install a reputable antivirus.
Run a quick scan.
steps_linux: Install ClamAV and turn on automatic signature updates.
Scan your download folders regularly.

Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object Ant.effet: Shows the state of Microsoft Defender.

Start-MpScan -ScanType QuickScan.effet: Runs a quick scan (a few minutes).

sudo apt install clamav clamav-daemon.attention: Ubuntu / Debian. Fedora: sudo dnf install clamav

AV-002.title: Real-time protection disabled
AV-002.description: The antivirus is installed but does not scan files when they are opened or downloaded.
AV-002.danger: A malicious file can run before any scan.
AV-002.location: Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings
steps: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection.
Click “Manage settings”.
Turn on “Real-time protection”.

Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object Rea.effet: Shows whether real-time protection is on.

AV-003.title: Outdated antivirus signatures
AV-003.description: Virus definitions have not been updated for more than 7 days.
AV-003.location: Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Updates
steps: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection.
Click “Protection updates” > “Check for updates”.
steps_linux: Update the ClamAV signatures.
steps_macos: XProtect signatures arrive with automatic macOS updates: turn on “Install Security Responses and system files”.

Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object Ant.effet: Shows the date and age (in days) of the signatures.

open \"x-apple.systempreferences:com.app.effet: Opens Software Update: turn on “Install Security Responses and system files”.

ENC-001.title: System disk not encrypted (BitLocker off)
ENC-001.description: The disk holding Windows and your data is not encrypted.
ENC-001.danger: If the computer is lost or stolen, anyone can read the whole disk by plugging it into another machine, without knowing the Windows password.
ENC-001.impact: All personal and professional data leaks if the computer is stolen.
ENC-001.location: Control Panel > System and Security > BitLocker Drive Encryption
ENC-001.description_linux: The disk holding the system and your data is not encrypted.
ENC-001.danger_linux: If the computer is lost or stolen, anyone can read the whole disk by plugging it into another machine, without knowing the login password.
ENC-001.description_macos: The disk holding the system and your data is not encrypted.
ENC-001.danger_macos: If the computer is lost or stolen, anyone can read the whole disk by plugging it into another machine, without knowing the login password.
steps: Open “Manage BitLocker” from the Start menu.
Click “Turn on BitLocker” for drive C:.
Back up the recovery key (Microsoft account, file on a USB stick or printout), NEVER only on the encrypted disk.
Choose “Encrypt used disk space only” and “New encryption mode”.
Restart to start encryption (the PC stays usable meanwhile).
steps_linux: LUKS encryption is normally chosen at installation: back up your data.
Reinstall the distribution with “Encrypt the installation” checked (LVM + LUKS).
Restore your data.
steps_macos: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security.
Click “Turn On” in the FileVault section.
Keep the recovery key in a safe place (or link it to your iCloud account).

manage-bde -status C:.effet: Shows the BitLocker state of drive C:.

control /name Microsoft.BitLockerDriveEn.effet: Opens “Manage BitLocker” (recommended method: the wizard guides every step).

manage-bde -on C: -RecoveryPassword.effet: Creates a recovery key and starts encrypting C: (the computer stays usable).
manage-bde -on C: -RecoveryPassword.attention: BEFORE: write down the recovery key shown (48 digits) and keep it off this PC (paper, photo, Microsoft account). Without it, your data can be lost. Windows Home: BitLocker doesn't exist, use “Device encryption” in Settings.

lsblk -f.effet: Shows the disks and their encryption.

open \"x-apple.systempreferences:com.app.effet: Opens Privacy & Security, FileVault section (recommended method).

sudo fdesetup enable.effet: Turns on FileVault and shows the recovery key.
sudo fdesetup enable.attention: Write down the recovery key shown and keep it off this Mac.

ENC-002.title: Data volume not encrypted
ENC-002.description: A secondary data disk or partition is not encrypted.
ENC-002.danger: The files on this volume can be read if the hardware is stolen.
ENC-002.impact: Leak of the data stored on this volume.
steps: Open “Manage BitLocker”.
Turn on BitLocker for the volume shown and back up the recovery key.

manage-bde -status.effet: Shows the BitLocker state of each disk.

manage-bde -on LETTRE: -RecoveryPassword.attention: Write down the recovery key shown and keep it off this PC.

remplacer.LETTRE: the drive letter shown in the finding (e.g. D)

APP-001.title: Software no longer supported
APP-001.description: This software (or this version branch) no longer receives security fixes from its publisher.
APP-001.danger: Flaws that are discovered will never be fixed; outdated software is a classic entry point.
steps: Check whether the software is still used.
If not: uninstall it (Settings > Apps).
If it is: install the latest supported version from the publisher's official website, then uninstall the old one.
steps_linux: Update to a supported branch (newer package from the distribution, or a distribution upgrade).
Uninstall the package if it is no longer used.
steps_macos: Update the app from the App Store, its “Check for Updates” menu or Homebrew.
Delete it if it is no longer used.

winget list --name \"NOM_DU_LOGICIEL\".effet: Checks that the software is installed and shows its version.
winget list --name \"NOM_DU_LOGICIEL\".attendu: the current version, or nothing if it was uninstalled

remplacer.NOM_DU_LOGICIEL: the software name shown in the finding (e.g. Visual C++ 2010)

start ms-settings:appsfeatures.effet: Opens the list of installed apps (Uninstall or Modify).

winget upgrade --name \"NOM_DU_LOGICIEL\.effet: Installs the latest version of the software.

remplacer.NOM_DU_LOGICIEL: the software name shown in the finding

winget uninstall --name \"NOM_DU_LOGICIE.effet: Uninstalls the software, if you no longer use it.
winget uninstall --name \"NOM_DU_LOGICIE.attention: First check that no program needs it (Visual C++ components are sometimes used by other software).

remplacer.NOM_DU_LOGICIEL: the software name shown in the finding

apt list --installed 2>/dev/null | grep.effet: Shows the package and its version.

remplacer.NOM: the package name shown in the finding

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade.effet: Updates packages to the latest version provided by the distribution.

sudo apt remove NOM.effet: Uninstalls the package if it is no longer used.

remplacer.NOM: the package name shown in the finding

open -a \"App Store\".effet: Opens the App Store, Updates tab.

brew upgrade.effet: Updates the software installed with Homebrew.

APP-002.title: Update available
APP-002.description: A newer version of this software is available in the same supported branch.
APP-002.danger: Minor updates often fix security flaws.
APP-002.impact: Vulnerabilities already fixed by the publisher but still present on the computer.
steps: Open the software and use its “Check for updates” feature, or use winget.
Turn on automatic updates if available.
steps_linux: Update the packages.
steps_macos: Update the app (App Store, the app's menu or Homebrew).

winget upgrade.effet: Lists the software with an update available.

remplacer.NOM_DU_LOGICIEL: the software name shown in the finding

winget upgrade --all.effet: Updates all the software in the list.

brew upgrade.effet: Updates Homebrew software; for others: App Store > Updates.

APP-003.title: Several versions of the same software installed
APP-003.description: Several versions of the same software coexist (e.g. Java 8, 11 and 17).
APP-003.danger: Old versions remain exploitable even if you no longer use them, and they take up disk space.
APP-003.impact: Needless attack surface, wasted disk space, confusion between versions.
steps: Identify the version your projects actually use.
Uninstall the other versions.
steps_linux: Identify the version your projects use.
Remove the other packages.
steps_macos: Remove unused versions (drag the app to the Trash, or brew uninstall).

winget list --name \"NOM\".effet: Lists every installed version with its identifier (ID column).

start ms-settings:appsfeatures.effet: Opens the list of apps to uninstall the old version.

winget uninstall --id IDENTIFIANT.attention: Keep the version your projects use.

remplacer.IDENTIFIANT: the ID column of the version to remove

remplacer.PAQUET: the exact name of the package to remove

sudo apt autoremove.effet: Removes dependencies that are no longer needed.

brew list --versions.effet: Lists Homebrew software and their versions.

brew cleanup.effet: Removes old versions kept by Homebrew.

APP-004.title: Large applications
APP-004.description: Installed applications taking more than 2 GB according to what they declare in the registry.
APP-004.danger: No security risk, but you could free space if they are no longer used.
APP-004.location: Settings > Apps > Installed apps (sort by size)
steps: Sort the applications by size.
Uninstall the ones you no longer use.

start ms-settings:appsfeatures.effet: Opens the list of apps: sort by size and uninstall the ones you no longer use.

open /Applications.effet: Opens the Applications folder (dragging an app to the Trash uninstalls it).

PERF-001.title: Processor saturated
PERF-001.description: Average processor use is above 85% during the measurement.
PERF-001.danger: No direct security risk; however, unexplained saturation can be a sign of malware (e.g. cryptocurrency mining).
steps: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc).
Sort by “CPU” and identify the program responsible (see the list of heavy processes).
Close or uninstall the program if it isn't needed; run an antivirus scan if the process is unknown.

taskmgr.effet: Opens Task Manager: click the “CPU” column to sort.

Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descendin.effet: Lists the 10 programs that used the processor the most.

PERF-002.title: Not enough memory (RAM)
PERF-002.description: The computer has less than 8 GB of RAM, below the recommendation for everyday use today.
PERF-002.impact: The disk swap file is used, causing major slowdowns.
steps: Check how many memory slots are free (CPU-Z app or the manufacturer's spec sheet).
Add a compatible memory module to reach at least 8 GB (ideally 16 GB).
Meanwhile, limit the number of apps open at the same time.

Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory | S.effet: Shows each memory module (size in bytes, speed, slot).

PERF-003.title: Memory almost full
PERF-003.description: More than 85% of RAM is in use at the time of the scan.
steps: Close unused apps and browser tabs.
Identify the heaviest programs (see the list).
Disable unnecessary startup programs.

taskmgr.effet: Opens Task Manager: sort by “Memory” and close what you don't need.

Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet64 -.effet: Lists the 10 programs using the most memory.

PERF-004.title: Many programs launched at startup
PERF-004.description: Several programs start automatically when you sign in.
PERF-004.danger: Startup programs are also a way for malware to persist: every unknown entry should be checked.
PERF-004.impact: Slower startup and memory permanently in use.
steps: Open Task Manager > “Startup” tab.
Disable non-essential programs (keep the antivirus and drivers).
Search the web for any unknown entry before disabling it.
steps_linux: Open “Startup Applications” (GNOME Tweaks or your desktop settings).
Disable non-essential applications.
steps_macos: Open System Settings > General > Login Items.
Remove unneeded items and turn off “Allow in the Background” for unnecessary apps.

start ms-settings:startupapps.effet: Opens Settings > Apps > Startup: one switch per program.

taskmgr /0 /startup.effet: Opens the Task Manager “Startup” tab directly.

Get-CimInstance Win32_StartupCommand | S.effet: Lists the programs launched at startup.

ls ~/.config/autostart.effet: Lists the applications launched when you sign in.

PERF-005.title: Application using a lot of memory
PERF-005.description: An application (all its processes together) uses more than 20% of RAM.
steps: Check whether the application needs to run all the time.
Reduce its use (fewer tabs, extensions or open projects) or restart it.

Get-Process -Name NOM | Measure-Object W.effet: Shows the total memory used by this application (Sum, in bytes).

remplacer.NOM: the application name without “.exe” (e.g. Code, chrome)

taskmgr.effet: Opens Task Manager to close or restart the application.

PERF-006.title: Computer not restarted for a long time
PERF-006.description: The computer has not been restarted for more than 14 days.
PERF-006.danger: Some security fixes only apply after a restart.
steps: Save your work and restart the computer (Restart, not Shut down: fast startup doesn't reset everything).
steps_linux: Restart to apply kernel updates.
steps_macos: Apple menu > Restart.

shutdown /r /t 0.attention: Save your work: the computer restarts immediately.

cat /var/run/reboot-required.effet: Shows whether updates are asking for a restart.

sudo reboot.attention: Save your work: the computer restarts immediately.

sudo shutdown -r now.attention: Save your work: the computer restarts immediately.

PERF-007.title: System installed on a mechanical disk (HDD)
PERF-007.description: The main disk is a mechanical hard drive, much slower than an SSD.
PERF-007.impact: Slow startup and slow app launches.
steps: Replace the disk with an SSD and clone the system (Macrium Reflect, Clonezilla, manufacturer's tool).

Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object Friendl.effet: Shows whether each disk is an SSD or an HDD.

STO-001.title: Low disk space
STO-001.description: The partition has less than 20% free space.
STO-001.danger: Windows updates can fail for lack of space, which indirectly creates a security risk.
STO-001.danger_linux: System updates can fail for lack of space, which indirectly creates a security risk.
STO-001.danger_macos: System updates can fail for lack of space, which indirectly creates a security risk.
steps: Open Settings > System > Storage and run “Cleanup recommendations”.
Delete the duplicate files and large unneeded files listed by KMB.
Empty the Recycle Bin and the Downloads folder.
Turn on Storage Sense.
steps_linux: Clean the package cache and old kernels.
Delete duplicates and large files listed by KMB.
Empty the trash and shrink the logs.
steps_macos: Open System Settings > General > Storage and follow the recommendations.
Delete duplicates and large files listed by KMB.
Empty the Trash.

start ms-settings:storagesense.effet: Opens Settings > Storage: “Cleanup recommendations” and Storage Sense.

cleanmgr /d C:.effet: Opens Disk Cleanup: check what you want to delete (temporary files, Recycle Bin…).
cleanmgr /d C:.attention: Also click “Clean up system files” to free more space.

sudo apt autoremove && sudo apt clean.effet: Removes unneeded packages and cached copies of installed ones.

sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=200M.effet: Shrinks the system logs to 200 MB.

open \"x-apple.systempreferences:com.app.effet: Opens Settings > General > Storage and its recommendations.

STO-002.title: Duplicate files
STO-002.description: Files with exactly the same content (same SHA-256 fingerprint) exist in several places.
STO-002.impact: Wasted disk space and confusion between versions of the same file.
STO-002.location: See the list of duplicate groups in the Storage tab
steps: Look at the list of duplicates (the oldest file is shown first).
Keep a single copy, in the most logical place.
Delete the other copies, then empty the Recycle Bin.

Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 'CHEMIN1'.effet: Computes the fingerprint of two files to confirm they are identical.

remplacer.CHEMIN1: the full path of the 1st file (right-click the file > Copy as path)
remplacer.CHEMIN2: the full path of the 2nd file

explorer.effet: Opens File Explorer: delete the copies (✗ in the site's list) and keep the original (✓).

sha256sum \"CHEMIN1\" \"CHEMIN2\".effet: Computes the fingerprint of two files.

shasum -a 256 \"CHEMIN1\" \"CHEMIN2\".effet: Computes the fingerprint of two files.

STO-003.title: Large files
STO-003.description: Files over 500 MB stored locally in your personal folders.
STO-003.impact: Space you could free (installers already used, videos, archives).
STO-003.location: See the list in the Storage tab
steps: Delete installers (.exe, .msi) you have already used.
Move videos and archives to an external drive or online storage.

Get-ChildItem $env:USERPROFILE -File -Re.effet: Lists the files over 1 GB in your profile (can take a minute).

explorer.effet: Opens File Explorer to move these files to an external drive or delete them.

find ~ -type f -size +1G -exec ls -lh {}.effet: Lists the files over 1 GB in your home folder.

STO-004.title: Large Downloads folder
STO-004.description: The Downloads folder takes more than 5 GB.
STO-004.danger: Old installers can be run again by mistake.
steps: Sort the Downloads folder by size.
Delete installers and archives you have already used.
Turn on automatic Downloads cleanup in Storage Sense.

explorer shell:Downloads.effet: Opens the Downloads folder: sort by size and delete installers you have already used.

STO-005.title: Physical disk in poor health
STO-005.description: Windows reports a degraded health state (SMART) for a physical disk.
STO-005.description_linux: The system reports a degraded health state (SMART) for a physical disk.
STO-005.description_macos: The system reports a degraded health state (SMART) for a physical disk.
steps: Back up important data immediately.
Check the state with CrystalDiskInfo.
Replace the disk.
steps_linux: Back up immediately.
Read the detailed SMART report.
Replace the disk.
steps_macos: Back up immediately (Time Machine).
Check the disk with Disk Utility > First Aid.
Have the disk replaced.

Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object Friendl.effet: Shows the health state of each disk.

sudo smartctl -H /dev/sda.effet: Shows the disk's SMART health check.

remplacer.sda: the disk name (see the lsblk command)

diskutil info / | grep SMART.effet: Shows the SMART state of the startup disk.

LNX-001.title: Account other than root with UID 0
LNX-001.description: An account other than root has ID 0, which means full control of the system.
LNX-001.danger: This is a classic backdoor technique: a discreet account with root powers.
LNX-001.impact: Full control of the system by an unmonitored account.
steps: Check who created this account and why.
If the account is not legitimate: lock it immediately, then analyse the system.
Otherwise: give it a normal UID and use sudo.

awk -F: '$3 == 0 {print $1}' /etc/passwd.effet: Lists the accounts with full control (UID 0).

sudo usermod -L NOM.attention: Then analyse the system: this account may be a backdoor.

remplacer.NOM: the account name shown in the finding

LNX-002.title: Direct SSH login as root allowed
LNX-002.description: The SSH server accepts direct password logins to the root account.
LNX-002.danger: The root account exists on every Linux machine: it is the first target of bots trying passwords.
LNX-002.impact: Full takeover if the root password is guessed.
steps: Open /etc/ssh/sshd_config.
Set “PermitRootLogin no” (or “prohibit-password”).
Restart the SSH service and check that another account with sudo can log in.

sudo sshd -T | grep -i permitrootlogin.effet: Shows whether root can log in over SSH.

sudo sed -i 's/^#\\?PermitRootLogin.*/Pe.effet: Forbids direct root login over SSH.

sudo systemctl restart ssh || sudo syste.effet: Restarts SSH to apply the change.
sudo systemctl restart ssh || sudo syste.attention: Check that another account with sudo can log in before closing your session.

LNX-003.title: SSH password authentication enabled
LNX-003.description: The running SSH server accepts passwords instead of requiring keys.
LNX-003.danger: Passwords can be guessed by brute force; SSH keys are practically impossible to guess.
LNX-003.impact: Remote access to the computer if a password is weak.
steps: Create a key pair on your client computer (ssh-keygen) and copy it (ssh-copy-id).
Check that key login works.
Set “PasswordAuthentication no”, then restart SSH.

ssh-keygen -t ed25519.effet: Run on the computer that connects: creates a key pair (press Enter to accept the defaults).

ssh-copy-id utilisateur@serveur.effet: Copies your key to this PC.

remplacer.utilisateur@serveur: your account and this PC's address

sudo sed -i 's/^#\\?PasswordAuthenticati.attention: Test key login FIRST, otherwise you could lose remote access.

sudo systemctl restart ssh || sudo syste.effet: Restarts SSH to apply the change.

LNX-004.title: No confinement module active (SELinux / AppArmor)
LNX-004.description: Neither SELinux in “enforcing” mode nor AppArmor is active. These modules limit what each program is allowed to do.
LNX-004.danger: A compromised program (browser, web server) can reach everything its user can reach.
steps: Ubuntu/Debian: check that AppArmor is installed and enabled.
Fedora/RHEL: set SELinux to enforcing mode in /etc/selinux/config.
Restart and check.

sudo setenforce 1.effet: Sets SELinux to “Enforcing” until the next restart (to make it permanent: /etc/selinux/config).

MAC-001.title: Gatekeeper disabled
MAC-001.description: Gatekeeper checks that downloaded apps are signed and notarized by Apple. It is disabled.
MAC-001.danger: Any app, including malware, can open without warning.
steps: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security.
Under “Allow applications downloaded from”, choose “App Store and identified developers”.

MAC-002.title: System Integrity Protection (SIP) disabled
MAC-002.description: SIP prevents any change to macOS system files, even by the administrator. It is disabled.
MAC-002.danger: Malware that obtained administrator rights can deeply modify macOS and hide in it.
steps: Restart in Recovery mode (hold the power button on Apple silicon, Cmd+R on Intel).
Open Utilities > Terminal.
Type “csrutil enable”, then restart.

csrutil status.effet: Shows whether System Integrity Protection (SIP) is active.

csrutil enable.effet: Turns SIP back on: type it in the Terminal of RECOVERY MODE, then restart.
csrutil enable.attention: Doesn't work in a normal session: start in Recovery mode first.

MAC-003.title: Automatic security updates disabled
MAC-003.description: macOS does not automatically check for updates or does not automatically install security fixes.
MAC-003.danger: Fixes for actively exploited flaws are installed late.
MAC-003.location: System Settings > General > Software Update > Automatic Updates
steps: Open System Settings > General > Software Update.
Click the (i) icon next to “Automatic updates”.
Turn on every option, especially “Install Security Responses and system files”.

defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.a.effet: Shows whether the automatic check is on.

sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences.effet: Turns on the automatic update check.
Turns on automatic installation of security fixes.

MAC-004.title: Automatic login enabled
MAC-004.description: The Mac signs in at startup without asking for a password.
MAC-004.danger: Anyone who turns on the Mac gets straight into the session and its data.
MAC-004.impact: Access to data in case of theft or physical access; incompatible with FileVault.
MAC-004.location: System Settings > Users & Groups > Automatically log in as
steps: Open System Settings > Users & Groups.
Set “Automatically log in as” to “Off”.

defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.a.effet: Shows the account that logs in automatically.

MAC-005.title: Firewall stealth mode disabled
MAC-005.description: In stealth mode, the Mac doesn't answer network probes (ping, port scans).
MAC-005.danger: The Mac is easier to spot on a public network.
MAC-005.impact: Slightly greater exposure on public networks.
steps: Open System Settings > Network > Firewall > Options.
Turn on “Enable stealth mode”.

/usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketf.effet: Shows whether stealth mode is on.

NET-006.title: Remote access enabled (SSH or Screen Sharing)
NET-006.description: The computer accepts remote connections (SSH session or screen sharing).
NET-006.danger: Anyone on the network can try to connect and guess a password.
NET-006.impact: Remote takeover if a password is weak.
steps: Open System Settings > General > Sharing.
Turn off “Remote Login” and “Screen Sharing” if they are not used.
Otherwise, limit access to specific users.

sudo systemsetup -getremotelogin.effet: Shows whether Remote Login (SSH) is on.

open \"x-apple.systempreferences:com.app.effet: Opens Settings > General > Sharing to turn off what isn't used.

WIFI-001.title: Connected to an open (unencrypted) Wi-Fi network
WIFI-001.description: The Wi-Fi network in use does not encrypt communications.
WIFI-001.danger: Anyone nearby can intercept unencrypted traffic; a fake access point with the same name is easy to create.
WIFI-001.impact: Theft of data and sessions, man-in-the-middle attacks.
steps: Disconnect from this network as soon as possible.
Use a protected network (WPA2 or WPA3) or your phone's hotspot.
Failing that, use a VPN and only HTTPS websites.

netsh wlan show interfaces.effet: Shows the connected Wi-Fi network and its protection (“Authentication” line).

netsh wlan disconnect.effet: Disconnects from the current Wi-Fi network.

nmcli -f IN-USE,SSID,SECURITY dev wifi.effet: Shows the connected network (*) and its protection.

WIFI-002.title: Wi-Fi network protected by obsolete encryption (WEP / WPA)
WIFI-002.description: The connected Wi-Fi network uses WEP or WPA (TKIP), protections broken for years.
WIFI-002.danger: A WEP password can be recovered in minutes; WPA/TKIP is also vulnerable.
WIFI-002.impact: Traffic interception and access to the local network by others.
steps: Open the router's administration page (often http://192.168.0.1 or http://192.168.1.1).
In the Wi-Fi / Security section, choose WPA2-AES or, better, WPA3.
Set a long Wi-Fi password (at least 12 characters).
Reconnect your devices.

netsh wlan show interfaces.effet: Shows the protection of the connected network (“Authentication” and “Cipher” lines).

nmcli -f IN-USE,SSID,SECURITY dev wifi.effet: Shows the protection of the connected network.

WIFI-003.title: Open network remembered with automatic connection
WIFI-003.description: An open Wi-Fi network is remembered and the computer reconnects to it automatically.
WIFI-003.danger: An attacker can create an access point with the same name: the computer will connect to it on its own.
WIFI-003.impact: Traffic interception without the user noticing.
steps: Open the list of known networks.
Remove (“Forget”) the network shown or turn off automatic connection.

remplacer.NOM: the network name shown in the finding
the network name shown in the finding
the network name shown in the finding

HW-001.title: Worn battery
HW-001.description: The battery's current maximum capacity is well below its original capacity.
HW-001.danger: No security risk; however, a very worn battery can swell.
steps: Read the battery report to confirm the wear.
Plan to replace the battery below 60% of its original capacity.
Avoid keeping the battery at 100% all the time (optimized charging option).

powercfg /batteryreport.effet: Creates battery-report.html in the folder shown: open it and compare DESIGN CAPACITY (original) and FULL CHARGE CAPACITY (current).
powercfg /batteryreport.attendu: a current capacity above 80% of the original

HW-002.title: High processor temperature
HW-002.description: A temperature sensor is above 90 °C at the time of the scan.
HW-002.impact: Slowdowns (the processor lowers its speed), faster wear, shutdowns.
steps: Clean the air vents and the fan (compressed air).
Use the laptop on a hard surface.
Identify the processes saturating the processor.

top.effet: Shows the programs using the processor the most (press q to quit).

STO-006.title: Space you can free safely
STO-006.description: Temporary files, browser caches, the Recycle Bin, old installers and already-installed updates take up space for nothing.
STO-006.danger: No security risk. These files are recreated as needed by the system or apps: deleting them loses nothing important.
STO-006.impact: Wasted disk space; a disk that is too full slows the computer down and can block updates.
steps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check “Temporary files”, “Recycle Bin”, “Thumbnails” and “Windows Update Cleanup”.
Click “Remove files”.
In your browser: Settings > Privacy > Clear browsing data > Cached images and files.
steps_linux: Empty the trash.
Delete the contents of ~/.cache (apps recreate it).
Clean the package cache.
steps_macos: Empty the Trash.
Quit your apps, then empty ~/Library/Caches.
Settings > General > Storage: follow the recommendations.

start ms-settings:storagesense.effet: Opens Settings > Storage > Temporary files: check the items, then “Remove files”.

cleanmgr /d C:.effet: Opens Disk Cleanup (temporary files, thumbnails, error reports, old updates).
cleanmgr /d C:.attention: Click “Clean up system files” to include old Windows updates.

Remove-Item \"$env:TEMP\\*\" -Recurse -F.effet: Empties your account's temporary files folder (files in use are skipped).

Clear-RecycleBin -Force.attention: The files in the Recycle Bin will be permanently deleted.

du -sh ~/.cache ~/.local/share/Trash 2>/.effet: Shows the size of the cache and the trash.

rm -rf ~/.cache/*.effet: Empties the application cache (it rebuilds itself).

gio trash --empty.attention: The files in the trash will be permanently deleted.

sudo apt clean.effet: Removes cached copies of packages already installed.

du -sh ~/Library/Caches ~/.Trash.effet: Shows the size of the caches and the Trash.

rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/*.effet: Empties the application caches (they rebuild themselves).
